rgb: This indoor studio scene places the camera wearer on a white floor backdrop, holding an open notebook and pen within arm’s reach, roughly 0.25 to 0.6 m ahead and below eye level. In frames 1 and 2, a person crouches on the studio floor around 2.5 to 3 m ahead and slightly left, facing and looking straight at the wearer while holding a camera to their face. A circular reflector stand is immediately behind that person on the left, about 3.5 m away, while two standing people are visible 5 to 6 m away in the background. An illuminated orange softbox and stand sit about 1.5 to 2 m away on the right and front-right; a red step ladder rests against the right wall at approximately 2.5 to 3 m; and a table with stools is farther along that wall, about 3.5 to 4.5 m from the wearer. From frame 1 to frame 4, the wearer angles their head downward and moves the open notebook toward the camera, reaching about 0.25 m in frames 3 and 4. The notebook then blocks the middle of the white backdrop, while the background people, reflector, and all of the crouching photographer except their feet leave the view above the frame’s top edge. In frame 5, the notebook drops back to about 0.5 m and the viewpoint moves slightly downward, pushing the crouching photographer entirely beyond the top edge while exposing the hands and legs of a seated person in blue directly to the wearer’s left, within arm’s reach at about 0.4 m and partly cropped by the bottom-left boundary.
depth: The depth map represents the studio’s continuous three-dimensional structure, including a smooth brightness transition over the white floor sheet from about 0.5 m beneath the camera wearer to 2 m ahead. On the right, this surface is bordered by a studio-light stand and stepladder 1.5–3 m away, while a crouching photographer faces the wearer from the front-left at 2.5–3 m, positioned before a circular diffuser at 3–3.5 m; background people and furniture lie farther away at 4–5.5 m. At the bottom of the view and within arm’s reach, 0.2–0.5 m away, the wearer’s open notebook and right hand gripping a pen form the brightest foreground surfaces. A seated person’s arms and legs also appear roughly 0.5 m away at the bottom-left in frames 2 and 5. Over the five frames, the wearer tips their head down and raises the notebook to 0.2–0.3 m in frames 3–4, then lowers it to 0.4–0.5 m in frame 5. As a result, the bright notebook plane grows across and conceals the middle-distance floor, while the crouching photographer shifts beyond the top of the image. Unlike the RGB strip, where the textureless white pages and uniformly white floor backdrop visually merge, the depth view distinguishes the angled notebook plane from the floor beneath it in frames 1, 2, and 5 and exposes the continuous ground incline. Nevertheless, depth is inaccurate for the intensely illuminated studio lamp at the far right, which becomes pure white in frames 1, 2, and 5 as though it were at zero distance. It also fuses the raised notebook’s upper boundary with the white floor sheet in frames 3–4 and drops the slender tripod legs and remote background figures into the dark far field.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view marks separate regions throughout the studio, distinguishing the foreground notebook and floor sheet from the crouching photographer, who faces the wearer from 2.5–3 m away on the front-left. It also separates two distant standing people located 4.5–5.5 m behind the photographer in frame 2 and the studio gear arranged along the right side at distances of 1.5–3.5 m. Inside the wearer’s arm’s reach, 0.2–0.5 m away, the map segments the right hand holding the pen at the bottom-right in frames 3–5 and the left hand in frame 5, together with the seated neighbor’s arm and legs roughly 0.5 m away at the bottom-left in frame 5. As the camera points sharply downward and the elevated notebook hides the room during frames 3–4 before being lowered again in frame 5, background masks move beyond the top boundary and foreground-person masks enter along the bottom. This contributes little beyond the RGB imagery, apart from separating the tiny, partly hidden standing figures at frame 2’s upper edge. Its semantic labels and object outlines are highly unreliable: in frame 2 it combines the white notebook with the floor backdrop into one enormous mask incorrectly called ‘bed,’ while frames 3–4 show the same area as an unlabeled purple polygon. It identifies the crouching photographer as ‘dog’ and ‘teddy bear’ in frame 2, and calls the circular diffuser, studio light, and red stepladder ‘chair’ in frames 1–2 or ‘traffic light’ and ‘umbrella’ in frame 5. The system additionally misses both the floor sheet and foreground notebook entirely in frames 1 and 5, does not detect the seated neighbor’s limbs in frame 2, and excludes the pen and narrow tripod stands throughout every frame.
pose: The body-and-hand skeleton display extracts only the human keypoints belonging to the crouching photographer, positioned 2.5–3 m ahead and a little left of the camera wearer near the white floor sheet’s far boundary. In frames 1 and 2, a compact yellow body skeleton depicts the photographer in a low squat, knees flexed, with elbows drawn inward within reach of their own upper body and camera, and with the shoulders and head directed squarely toward the wearer. Through the five-frame sequence, the wearer angles the viewpoint downward at the notebook, making the photographer’s skeleton travel upward toward the top-left between frames 1 and 2. By frame 3, the upper border crops it to only a small collection of foot keypoints in the top-left, and it vanishes completely from view in frames 4 and 5. Relative to the RGB strip, this overlay clearly communicates the photographer’s folded-limb arrangement and forward-facing stance even though dark clothing obscures detail and the handheld camera blocks their face. Everywhere else, however, the pose map is unreliable. It detects no magenta hand skeletons at all, entirely overlooking the wearer’s own hands as they hold the notebook and pen 0.2–0.5 m away in frames 3–5. It likewise misses the seated person’s arms and legs 0.5 m away at the bottom-left in frames 2 and 5, as well as both standing people situated 4.5–5.5 m away in the background during frames 1–2.
